Business owners

You've spent years building it. Let's find the right next chapter.

A change of ownership begins with a question about the future. Whether you founded the company or are thinking about succession with your family, your priorities shape the conversation.

Discuss your business confidentially ↗

How we help

  • Explore a full exit, a majority sale or a strategic partnership.
  • Decide what matters for your employees, customers and family after a sale.
  • Discuss appropriate successors and agree how and when introductions should happen.
  • Coordinate diligence, negotiations and a considered handover with your advisers.

Your journey

  1. Confidential conversation
  2. Understand your objectives
  3. Evaluate ownership options
  4. Identify suitable counterparties
  5. Facilitate execution

Common questions

What if our family is still deciding?

Start with the questions you are considering. We can explore what a successor, strategic buyer or continuing family role might look like before you settle on a route.

What should I share at the beginning?

Your sector, location, broad revenue range and what you would like to explore are enough. You can choose to discuss revenue privately and keep detailed financials for a later conversation.

When would a buyer learn our identity?

We first discuss your disclosure preferences and the purpose of an introduction. Sensitive information belongs in a later, agreed exchange with appropriate confidentiality arrangements.

Corporate acquirers

Your next stage of growth may already exist.

A company you acquire could bring a manufacturing capability, a distribution network or the team to enter a new region. We work with promoters, corporate development teams and international strategics to define what a target must add.

Share your acquisition thesis ↗

How we help

  • Translate your growth priority into a focused acquisition brief.
  • Originate off-market targets by sector, capability, geography and size.
  • Explore vertical integration, complementary product lines and sector consolidation.
  • Qualify owner interest and coordinate introductions and transaction workstreams.

Your journey

  1. Define your acquisition thesis
  2. Targeted origination
  3. Qualify opportunities
  4. Meet the owner
  5. Transaction support

Common questions

What makes an acquisition brief useful?

Specify the capability or market you want to add, target geography, indicative budget and preferred level of control. Identify the one or two criteria a target must meet.

Can we search for a series of acquisitions?

Yes. We can help distinguish the first platform business from later additions, then qualify targets against a common roll-up or consolidation strategy.

Can an overseas corporate submit a mandate?

Yes. Share the India entry or expansion objective and the kind of local business you are seeking. Cross-border structures require assessment by qualified legal, tax and regulatory advisers.

Investors & family offices

Capital meets businesses worth building upon.

A family office investing its own capital approaches ownership differently from a buyout fund or an operator-backed holding company. We start with your mandate, intended role and the businesses you know best.

Share your investment preferences ↗

How we help

  • Source established businesses against your ownership and sector preferences.
  • Explore direct acquisitions, investor-backed operators and search fund relationships.
  • Identify potential partners for India-focused acquisition strategies.
  • Coordinate introductions for your independent evaluation and diligence.

Your journey

  1. Understand your investment mandate
  2. Identify potential fit
  3. Qualified introductions
  4. Independent evaluation
  5. Transaction support

Common questions

Who can share investment preferences?

Family offices, private equity and micro private equity firms, holding companies, search fund investors, experienced individual investors and international investment teams can share a mandate.

Am I subscribing to an investment?

This enquiry starts an advisory conversation about your acquisition interests. Legacy Search facilitates introductions and transaction processes. Each investor independently assesses any opportunity.

Can we explore an operator-backed acquisition?

Tell us the sectors you understand, your preferred role and the operator experience you seek. We can assess relevant business and operating relationships against those criteria.

Entrepreneurs & operators

You don't always have to build from zero.

Entrepreneurship through acquisition means buying a company and running it. An established business brings customers, a team and years of operating knowledge. Your experience shapes what you can contribute as its next owner.

Explore becoming an acquisition entrepreneur ↗

How we help

  • Define a search around your operating experience and sector knowledge.
  • Explore acquiring and running a business independently or with investor backing.
  • Consider management-led buyouts and founder succession opportunities.
  • Meet owners and potential partners where your ambitions and capabilities align.

Your journey

  1. Understand your operating experience
  2. Define acquisition interests
  3. Assess alignment
  4. Explore opportunities and partnerships

Common questions

Do I need a search fund to start?

You can begin as an independent operator, entrepreneur, senior executive or industry specialist. Tell us the business you would be equipped to lead and what support you would need.

What should I include about my background?

Share the sectors, teams, plants, products or business units you have run, along with your preferred region and level of ownership involvement.

What happens after I enquire?

We review your interests for fit with owners, businesses or potential partners. Conversations depend on mutual interest. Employment, funding and an acquisition are not guaranteed.

Deal scouts & partners

Opportunity is everywhere. Help us discover it.

Industry professionals often hear a founder’s succession question long before a sale process begins. Our pan-India network of 250+ active deal scouts connects that local knowledge with an acquisition team.

Become a deal scout ↗Introduce an opportunity ↗

How we help

  • Introduce an owner considering a transition or a corporate with an acquisition brief.
  • Identify acquisition-oriented investors and industry-specific consolidation opportunities.
  • Bring context from your work as an adviser, chartered accountant, consultant or industry professional.
  • Agree the scope of collaboration and introduction terms before sharing an opportunity.

Your journey

  1. Register interest
  2. Profile evaluation
  3. Onboarding and agreed terms
  4. Introduce an opportunity
  5. Qualification
  6. Collaboration

Common questions

Can I introduce a single opportunity?

Yes. Use “Introduce an opportunity” and describe the sector, geography and broad ownership objective. Keep identifying details private until you have permission to share them.

Who can join the network?

We welcome industry professionals, business advisers, entrepreneurs, association members and people developing an interest in M&A origination. We review each profile for fit.

How are commercial terms decided?

Any commercial arrangement is governed by separately agreed terms. The introductory conversation establishes your role, the scope of work and how an opportunity will be evaluated.
